deck_title: Savart-Taylor R_bell = rho*Q*v0/(4*pi*sigma) liquid bell sheet radial expansion vs naive unscaled capillary sheet rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Félix Savart (1833) & G. I. Taylor (1959) impinging liquid-jet water-bell radial expansion law (balancing outward radial momentum flux rho * Q * v_0 against two-sided capillary rim pull 4 * pi * sigma * R_bell so R_bell = rho * Q * v_0 / (4 * pi * sigma) = R_0 / (1 + u), locking R_active / R_Savart = 1.0000x across all 17 capillary stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive unscaled ballistic sheet shader (keeping R = R_0 regardless of surface tension sigma(u) = sigma_0 * (1 + u), which overshoots the Savart-Taylor water-bell radius by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-sector radial momentum-capillary rim quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: 3D fountain mushroom domes, impinging water-jet splashes, spoon/plate sink water-bell sheets, and rocket impinging injector sprays
Computing the exact Taylor-Culick sonic rim termination radius R_bell = rho * Q * v_0 / (4 * pi * sigma) where h(R) = 2*sigma / (rho * v_0^2)
Coupling water-bell expansion directly to jet Weber number We_jet = rho * v_0^2 * R_jet / (2 * sigma)
not_for: Dry sand or gravel impacts with zero surface tension (sigma = 0)
Low-speed dripping faucets that never form a continuous radial sheet (We < 1)
